quotes.text: The new Usage Analytics API lets you build analytics dashboards for your end users. [Request to join the preview.]
Interested in getting early access to spend and credit balance alerts
You must [create a meter](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/usage-based/implementation-guide.md#create-meter) before you create an alert.
only triggers one time per customer, regardless of future usage.
We evaluate alerts when you report usage data after you create the alert. However, the evaluation includes usage data that you reported before you created the alert.

findings: The November 2026 page at https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/usage-based/alerts is a full 141-line usage alert guide, not a variant index. Its central behavior remains consistent with the May 2026 old capture: meter prerequisite; Dashboard/API alert creation for specific or all customers; one-time per-customer usage alert; billing.alert.triggered webhook; post-creation usage report evaluation including previously reported usage; max 25 alerts per meter/customer combination; no test-clock support (new lines 23–35, 39–60, 110–136; old lines 10–22, 26–55, 101–103, 127–129).

The new material addition is an invitation to request preview access to the Usage Analytics API and early access to spend and credit balance alerts, including a registration curl example (new lines 9–21; old line 8 only mentions Usage Analytics). The registration snippet is documentation content, not evidence that access was granted or that spend/credit-balance alerts are generally available or usable through the usage-alert endpoint. No registration action was taken.

The new API code example is curl instead of old Node, but both sample the same billing alert endpoint/alert_type=usage_threshold, customer filter, meter, gte=100, recurrence=one_time (new lines 49–61; old lines 35–57). The customer filter is an example scope, whereas the Dashboard defaults to Any customer and permits Specific customer (new lines 39–47). Do not infer that all-customer alerts require a customer filter or that 100 API calls is a required threshold.

The new webhook handler example is Ruby instead of old Node (new lines 63–118; old lines 59–111). The narrative still tells the application to verify the signature (new line 67). The Ruby sample verifies only if STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is nonempty and otherwise constructs an event from unsigned JSON (new lines 80–104); this branch must not be copied as proof of authenticated webhook delivery. billing.alert.triggered is the alert-specific event (new lines 110–113), not a PaymentIntent status check despite the generic code comment at new line 105.

Threshold wording uses both 'exceeds' and 'reaches' in prose; the API example explicitly uses usage_threshold[gte]=100 (new lines 23, 33–35, 59). Preserve the configured gte comparator and one-time per-customer recurrence rather than asserting a strict >100 boundary. The alert is evaluated when usage is reported after creation, but that evaluation includes pre-creation usage data (new line 134), so 'retroactive' should not be read as an immediate event at creation.

The current source captures the meter prerequisite, example API, webhook, and test-clock limitation (source lines 13–44), but omits the 25-per-meter/customer limit and post-creation-report evaluation condition retained in both raw versions. The new preview invitations also warrant a dated source update with no claim of live account entitlement.
substantive_changes: New preview-access documentation for Usage Analytics and early access to spend/credit-balance alerts (new lines 9–21 versus old line 8). This is a documented invitation, not an enabled alert capability.

No demonstrated change to the core one-time usage alert behavior, meter prerequisite, customer scoping, alert webhook, or limits (new lines 23–136; old lines 10–129). Node-to-curl alert API and Node-to-Ruby webhook examples are presentation/language changes (new lines 49–118; old lines 35–111).
historical_claims_to_preserve: The May 2026 one-time per-customer usage alert and meter prerequisite, with Dashboard all-customer or specific-customer selection and customer-filtered API example (old lines 10–55).

The May 2026 billing.alert.triggered event, signature-verification instruction, post-creation usage reporting trigger with prior data included, 25 meter/customer maximum, and test-clock incompatibility (old lines 59–63, 101–103, 123–129).

The distinction between usage alerts that notify and billing thresholds that can trigger invoices; the introductory sentence mentions both, but this page's procedure implements usage alerts (old lines 10–22; new lines 23–35).
conflicts: New line 105 says the webhook event type 'checks the status of PaymentIntents', but the branch at new lines 110–113 is billing.alert.triggered for a meter alert. Do not restate the generic comment as this alert's semantic effect.

New Ruby sample lines 80–104 parses unsigned JSON when STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is empty, whereas new line 67 directs signature verification. If a source summary discusses webhook authenticity, use the prose requirement and flag this sample fallback; do not recommend it as a secure production pattern.

Source line 19 and reciprocal wiki/concepts/stripe-usage-based-billing.md:142 say a customer 'first exceeds' threshold, while API sample uses gte=100 (new lines 35, 59). Keep prose tied to the configured gte threshold, and do not infer strict > rather than >=.

Source line 44 calls Usage Analytics merely mentioned; new line 9 offers preview access, while new lines 11–21 invite early access to distinct spend/credit-balance alerts. A source update should keep both preview/early-access qualifiers and avoid conflating them with the generally described meter usage alert.

Source line 42 retains test-clock limitation but omits the adjacent max-25 and post-creation usage-report condition (new lines 134–136; old lines 127–129). Reciprocal concept lines 139–142 include these limits and should remain consistent if source wording changes.
unresolved_questions: The invitation does not prove that a particular account received Usage Analytics preview access, or that spend and credit balance alerts are available. The page gives no schema or fulfillment behavior for those early-access alert types.
The page does not establish immediate alert firing at creation for historical usage; it only says a report after creation triggers evaluation that includes earlier reported usage.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/usage-based/alerts, the November capture establishes a meter prerequisite, Dashboard/API creation of one-time per-customer usage alerts, optional specific-customer scope, billing.alert.triggered notification, and limits (new lines 23–60, 110–136). The older May guide behind [[source-stripe-usage-based-billing-alerts-setup]] describes the same behavior (old lines 10–55, 101–129). Evaluation occurs when usage is reported after alert creation and includes previously reported usage; at most 25 alerts apply per meter/customer combination, and alerts do not work with test clocks (new lines 134–136). The new preview invitations are access requests, not proof of entitlement (new lines 9–21).
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/usage-based/alerts, the substantive documentation addition is preview request and early-access language for Usage Analytics and spend/credit-balance alerts (new lines 9–21; old line 8 mentioned Usage Analytics without an access link). [[source-stripe-usage-based-billing-alerts-setup]] should keep those dated qualifications and add the shared 25-alert limit and post-creation-report evaluation condition (new lines 134–136; old lines 127–129). The alert example changes from Node to curl and webhook example from Node to Ruby without changing the core usage-alert flow (new lines 49–118; old lines 35–111). The Ruby unsigned fallback conflicts with signature-verification prose, and gte=100 must not become a strict greater-than promise (new lines 59, 67, 80–113).
